text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Thursday.

- After a three-year recession, the construction sector sees a chink of light. In the coming year building output is expected to rise by 0.7 percent, compared with a forecast drop of 1.5 percent this year.
- Swiss telecommunications firm Swisscom will start offering services to Austrian firms. Southern Germany and Italy will follow.
- Two Bundeslaender-Versicherung shareholders, who voted against the insurer's plans to cut dividend payments to ordinary shareholders, are now turning to the courts.
- A road toll on heavy goods vehicles would hurt jobs, according to the Chamber of Economy. It considers further taxes on transport irresponsible.
- Salzburg is in a head-to-head race with Paris for a billion-schillings investment by Samsung.
- Grain prices have fallen sharply. Heavy rainfall has led to a deterioration in the quality of the grain harvest. Producer prices have fallen by up to 20 percent.
- Road and rail on a collision course. Austrian Railway's (OeBB) strategy of offering construction services to third parties has alarmed the construction sector. It is considering legal steps.
- The post office's mobile telephone network is growing. Motorola is rumoured favourite to win a contract to expand the network.
- Dollar strength raises the spectre of European interest rate rises. Bank Austria boss Randa sees no need for early action.
- Austria will introduce a telecommunications watchdog from November, in accordance with EU directives.
- Setting up a company will soon cost more. Parliament will consider raising numerous charges in the autumn.
